The Larco Museum was founded in the early 20th century and is housed in an 18th-century colonial-style residence of a Peruvian viceroy.

The collection includes ceramics, textiles, jewelry, gold objects, mummies and a large collection of pottery depicting erotic scenes. In total, the museum houses more than 45,000 exhibits connected with the history and everyday life of the Inca, Moche, Nazca and Chimú civilizations.

The visit costs $50 per person. The museum also has a restaurant serving national cuisine, Café del Muzeo.

Larco Museum houses collections devoted to Peru's ancient cultures, including ceramics and gold objects.

After visiting the museum, there is a break at a traditional tavern in the Pueblo Libre district, where you can sample a pisco-based drink.

The route then continues to Parque de la Reserva, home to the Magic Water Circuit, a complex of 13 illuminated fountains and water displays.

The excursion takes place on Nahuel Huapi Lake aboard a private 30-foot boat. The program includes stops at secluded beaches, opportunities to swim and paddleboards available on board.

The menu is chosen from the available options, such as sushi, ribeye steak or a selection of cheeses and smoked meats, accompanied by premium Argentine wine. At sunset, Bosque Gin cocktails and a cheese platter are served.

After the cruise, participants return to the chalet. In the Lakeshore Chalet program, this excursion takes one full day and is included in the overall trip price.

The excursion follows the shore of Lake Argentino and focuses on the region's history. Along the way, the guide tells you about Indigenous peoples and the first settlers who developed Patagonia.

The route reaches caves containing traces of the presence of Patagonia's Indigenous inhabitants and ancient rock art later discovered by researchers.

At the end of the trip, dinner is served in a cave. This is part of the evening excursion connected to the area's history, rather than a separate food-focused program.
